title: Does it make sense for pathlib PurePath objects to contain glob-style asterisk patterns?
q_body: I have some legacy Python code that uses strings for path operations which I'm migrating to using pathlib. One of these strings is a pattern that is used to find a specific type of file. I thought it would make sense to turn this into a pathlib PurePath since while it isn't actually a path that points to something on the filesystem, certain computational operations are useful to run on it, particularly expanduser() as in addition to containing glob-style asterisk patterns it may also contain tildes that need to be expanded into the user's actual home directory. However, glob.glob() crashes if you give it a PurePath : >>> glob.glob(p) Traceback (most recent call last): File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module> File "/usr/lib/python3.12/glob.py", line 28, in glob return list(iglob(pathname, root_dir=root_dir, dir_fd=dir_fd, recursive=recursive, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/lib/python3.12/glob.py", line 48, in iglob root_dir = pathname[:0] ~~~~~~~~^^^^ TypeError: 'PurePosixPath' object is not subscriptable This makes me wonder, does it even make sense in the first place to have glob-style asterisks in a pathlib PurePath? I tried reading the pathlib documentation but it doesn't really seem to specify what a PurePath should or shouldn't contain.
